profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at RackTop Systems

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Systems software design and development for our highly reliable, security-first storage platform.

positions.title: Developer Advocate
positions.description: As an illumos Advocate, I help people contribute new code and fixes to the operating system and ensure their work receives review and testing.

positions.title: Storage Architect
positions.description:
Helped build the top network storage appliance in the cloud.
Our platform provides highly available and cost effective network storage services and cloud migration using OpenZFS and tiered object storage.

positions.title: Kernel Engineer
positions.description:
I joined the Cerana (formerly Mistify) team at OmnTI to develop our in-house clustered platform for deploying containers and virtual networks on a datacenter scale.

Our platform was capable of self-constructing a cluster on bare metal and running applications using a Go-based secure isolation runtime I created with enhanced BPF (eBPF) syscall filtering. I introduced container-aware delegation for OpenZFS using Linux namespaces to provide secure multi-tenant access to storage management.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
On the Platform Software team at Nexenta, I worked on the operating system at the core of the NexentaStor storage appliance. I developed enhancements to fault tolerance and performance of the I/O stack, storage device drivers, and the ZFS filesystem.

I maintained the legacy Debian/Solaris platform and assisted with the NexentaStor project transition to the current illumos-based platform software.

Other areas of involvement include NFS and SMB file services, iSCSI, and the NDMP backup service. I also created reporting tools and processes for support staff.

positions.title: Application Engineer
positions.description:
Helped design and implement the scalable BitTorrent-based backend of a publishing platform for free media running on the Joyent cloud.

Non-blocking I/O improvements to popular free software libraries allowed our nodes to handle thousands of clients.
